items.transcript: So you've bought the Ninja Coffee Machine and you turn it on and you get this orange light next to the word clean. And you don't know what to clean so you ignore it. Well I'm going to tell you, you do need to do some cleaning but it's only going to take you 10 minutes. So I'm going to show you exactly what it's telling you to clean, how to clean it and what you need and then you're going to go and do it. It's going to be done and you're going to know how to do it for the future. And your £500 coffee machine is going to continue to give you after value because you're maintaining it the way you should. First things first I'm going to show you the state of mine. I'm going to clean all of this because what collects is the bits of coffee and then oils. You should find that if you've left this a long time the next coffee that you have afterwards tastes a little bit fresher. Before we start a couple of things that you'll need. I want you to go and look for this box. You got this when you purchased the coffee machine. Inside here is the tablet that we're going to use to clean this section of the coffee machine. Next you need to find this little cleaning tray here. Now this is going to hold the tablet and stop the water from filtering through when we clean the coffee machine. This could be in your box still or there's a little secret storage cupboard. You might have put it there. The last thing you need to check before you start the clean is that this has the double basket on. If you're not sure where it is it might again be sat in your accessory cupboard. And then two little bits of prep before the clean begins. You're going to want to empty your water tray because we're going to do a water cycle and it's going to fill up. And then you need to fill the water tank up to the max line. So we're going to pop our cleaning tray inside along with our tablet. Then lock that in and to start the clean you're going to want to press your cleaning button followed by your start brew button. So your timer here shows you how long it's going to take. It's five and a half minutes and then when it's ready we can check how it's done. So it's finished. Just be careful when you take it out because sometimes it does have a little bit of water in and it is hot. So be very careful. Then you're going to take this out like that and then we can do the rest of our cleaning. So we're going to empty the water tray because as you can see it is completely full. items.caption: Which use tissue to fold my clothes
items.transcript: Okay, let's talk about why I use tissue paper to fold my clothes. Now the first part of the answer is quite simply habit. From working in retail for so many years, folding clothes with tissue paper is just ingrained into my soul. However, there is a really practical reason why I still use this technique that translates really nicely from the shop floor to our homes. I fold the tissue paper to size judged on the type of storage that I'm going to use. So then instead of trying to judge where to fold the knitwear, I use the tissue paper as my guide. Sleeves in, fold around the paper, and every single one comes out pretty much the exact same size. So yes, the tissue paper does look really aesthetically pleasing, but the main thing is it saves me time because I'm doing the right fold first time. And yes, I do use the same piece of tissue paper over and over and over and over and over and over again.

items.transcript: So many questions yesterday asking what was this on my induction hob. These are hob protectors. My dad bought us these when we moved in because he couldn't, he was like you have to have these if you haven't got a non-scratch hob. They come on a roll and you cut them to size. These ones were a good size for us, I just had to cut them in half and we've got one on one side, one on the other. They withstand the heat up to 250 degrees Celsius so you do cook on them and they just give you a bit more confidence that you're not going to scratch your hob. They clean super easy, I just whack them in the washing machine and I feel like they also create extra space as well because now I'm not precious about what I put on top of the hob. I can put anything on there because we've got the hob protectors. Anyway, that's what they are and if you've got an induction hob, my dad says you have to have them.
